Minerals and Metals Working Group, Climate Change Industry Issues Table (1999). Cement and Concrete Options Paper. National Climate Change Process, Ottawa, October 1999. No report number, DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers ("page N of 14"; PDF page = printed + 1, cover unnumbered). Main file is thin: the Canadian average CO2 intensity per t cement (0.5 process, 0.35 combustion) and the capital cost of upgrading wet ($350/t) and long dry ($60/t) kilns to preheater/precalciner, with derived fuel-CO2 reductions from the printed fuel ratios (wet = 2x, long dry = 1.3x modern). No absolute specific energy per tonne is printed anywhere. Actions table (capital, NPV, Mt reduced, $/t) goes to measures; emissions series, fleet shares and relative fuel ratios to other-values. Not loaded: policy measure programme costs (IND-C&C-1/2/3: publicity, seminars), ICF and highway details beyond the measures rows. Traps: $/tonne upgrade cost denominator not stated (assumed per t annual capacity); no price year; numbers reprinted from the Hatch preliminary analysis; intensities are per t cement, not clinker.
